playbooks.title: Fix the phone menu (IVR)
playbooks.action: Call tickets are transferred 11.7 times per 100 vs 2.2 for other channels: rewrite the menu choices and confirm the issue with one spoken question before routing.
assumptions: the new menu is as accurate as the other channels' (19% of today's wrong choices remain)

message.text: Phone IVR customers experience 11.7 transfers per 100 tickets on average, compared to 2.2 transfers per 100 tickets for comparable tickets. This has impacted 9,725 tickets on the history days. Could your team please fix the phone menu (IVR)?

playbooks.title: Cross-train 2 Hindi-speaking agents on payment failure and refund
playbooks.action: Hindi payment failure and refund tickets wait 181 min vs 30 min. Train D11, D10 on payment failure and refund: they already speak Hindi and their shifts cover the hours no trained Hindi speaker works today.
assumptions: training is finished before the period and trained agents work at full speed

message.text: Hindi-speaking customers routed to Team B wait 181 min on average, against 29.9 min for comparable tickets; that is 2,568 tickets across the history days. To address this skill gap, please cross-train Hindi-speaking agents on payment failure and refund.

playbooks.title: Self-serve instant refund on weekend dinner (Team C)
playbooks.action: Team C is overloaded on weekend dinner. Offer an in-app instant refund for missing item claims on orders up to ₹300 in that window, so these customers need no agent.
assumptions: ASSUMPTION: 60% of eligible customers use self-serve
policy choice: only orders up to ₹300

message.text: Weekend dinner customers with Team C require 1.6× the agent-time on shift, against 1.0× the agent-time on shift for comparable tickets. That accounts for 1,700 tickets over the history days. Please implement self-serve instant refund on weekend dinner for Team C.

playbooks.title: Status banner the moment a spike alert fires
playbooks.action: Spikes like payment failure on day 18 come from one cause. When OpsLens raises a live spike alert, show an in-app status banner on that issue for 4 hours, so customers know it is being fixed.
assumptions: ASSUMPTION: 30% of customers who see the banner do not open a ticket

message.text: Payment failure customers logged 240 tickets a day during the Thursday September spike, against 100 tickets a day for comparable tickets. Across the history days, this problem group totaled 240 tickets. Please display a status banner the moment a spike alert fires.

playbooks.title: Self-serve instant refund on weekday night (Team B)
playbooks.action: Team B is overloaded on weekday night. Offer an in-app instant refund for refund claims on orders up to ₹300 in that window, so these customers need no agent.
assumptions: ASSUMPTION: 60% of eligible customers use self-serve
policy choice: only orders up to ₹300

message.text: Weekday night customers handled by Team B wait 145 min on average, compared to 42.9 min for comparable tickets; that is 656 tickets across the history days. Due to this capacity shortfall, could you please enable self-serve instant refunds on weekday nights for Team B?

playbooks.title: Kitchen order-check for restaurant cluster 17
playbooks.action: Cluster 17: 24.6% of its tickets are wrong item vs 9.4% elsewhere. Send the partners a quality alert and switch on order-check (packing photo before pickup) for this cluster.
assumptions: ASSUMPTION: 100% of the cluster's extra wrong item tickets go away

message.text: Customers ordering from restaurant cluster 17 experience 24.6% in wrong item tickets, against 9.4% for comparable tickets; that is 224 tickets. Please conduct a kitchen order-check for restaurant cluster 17.
